According to the latest issue of the "Power On" newsletter, Apple reportedly once considered adding a feature to Apple Upgrade that would have made the iPhone setup process virtually seamless: Apple would pre-copy your data over. However, this feature ultimately never came to fruition.

The concept is simple: since users would regularly upgrade their devices on a fixed monthly payment plan, why not make the transition process as simple as possible? Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported as such:

There are clearly a few loopholes here. First, your iCloud backup would be slightly out of date, since data transfer can only occur when the device is shipped out, lagging by a few days — unless you choose to pick it up in store.

In addition, there are obvious privacy concerns. Having said that, if you're already backing up to iCloud, it shouldn't be surprising that Apple holds your data. But for the average person, they might worry about how data is transferred to their new phone, and whether someone might have peeked at it during the process.

Two years ago, Apple rolled out a brand-new "Presto" system in its stores, allowing employees to update iPhones while they were still in the box. It's not hard to imagine this system being extended further to support iCloud backup transfers, with no one needing to view your data throughout the process.

That said, this feature ultimately never launched — and perhaps that's actually a good thing.
